items.summary: A multi-chiplet accelerator on TSMC's N2P node: up to 13.8 PFLOPS FP4, 288GB HBM4 across eight stacks at 18TB/s, 950W, 96 accelerators per rack and clusters of ~12,000, on a two-tier Ethernet fabric with a custom AI transport protocol. Microsoft claims 7x the rack-scale token throughput of Maia 200 and 40% more tokens per megawatt than leading GPU-based systems, with production deployment in 2027 as Azure's primary inference system; Reuters reports more than a million chips could ship in 2027. The GPU comparison baseline was not disclosed. Its memory appetite is the same demand squeezing consumer devices in [[2026-10-12#10|Apple's iPhone 18 Pro order cuts]].
items.title: Microsoft unveils Maia 300: 288GB HBM4, 7x rack throughput, multi-gigawatt Azure plans

items.summary: KlingAI Research aggregates each prompt's rewards into a shared reward-improving direction and adds a trust-region-masked second update, needing no differentiable reward model and no EMA tuning. On HunyuanVideo-13B with equally weighted visual and motion rewards it matches the late-stage mean reward of DiffusionNFT and Flow-GRPO-Fast using 12.02x and 11.72x fewer GPU hours, with 28.8% and 53.0% higher mean training rewards. It was the day's most-upvoted paper on Hugging Face.
items.title: DiffusionART cuts diffusion-model RL cost about 12x on a 13B video model

items.summary: A three-stage framework trains whole-body catching with RL, then infers a thrown box's dynamics from delayed partial observations, then recovers that representation from egocentric RGB-D while the controller stays fixed. It reaches 85.7% catch success in simulation from vision against 87.9% with privileged box state, and on a real Unitree G1 catches human throws 65% of the time at 2.5m and 40% at 5m — 76% and 59% of human catchers' rates. Removing temporal visual history costs 35.6 to 39.8 points.
items.title: Reflex catches thrown boxes on a humanoid from egocentric RGB-D alone

items.summary: An automated pipeline generates application designs, compiles them into runnable apps and repairs them through GUI-based evaluation, yielding 182 applications across 12 categories at a 91.5% mean task pass rate plus a 120-task benchmark. A computer-use agent trained on trajectories from these synthetic environments raises Pass@3 on the out-of-domain OSWorld benchmark from 41.39% to 56.97%. It is the training-data counterpart to the environment-scaling work in [[2026-10-11#6|AgentGarten]].
items.title: SoftwareGym synthesizes 182 GUI apps and lifts OSWorld Pass@3 from 41% to 57%

items.summary: The Apache-2.0 family extends the project's decision models to multimodal inputs, answering fixed sets of questions about a request in a single forward pass and loading through Transformers; weights are on Hugging Face. It is the open-weight entry in a niche that filled up in a week with [[2026-10-11#8|OpenAI's Decisions API]] and [[2026-10-12#7|Microsoft's Decision-1]].
items.title: vLLM Semantic Router releases Decision 3.0, six open multimodal decision models

items.summary: A 24 September directive had asked OpenAI and Anthropic to stop sharing new models with the UK AISI for pre-release safety testing; the US withdrew it on 11 October after 17 days, with access also covering Google DeepMind, following lobbying by UK AI minister Kanishka Narayan. It restores third-party pre-deployment testing at the moment Washington is making incident reporting mandatory in [[2026-10-11#2|the Super Intelligence Force rule]].
items.title: US reverses course and restores UK AI Security Institute access to frontier models

items.summary: Speaking in Singapore, Hock Tan and Lip-Bu Tan warned that the cost and availability of borrowing could constrain the buildout; Tan separately compared uninformed AI investors to casino gamblers and questioned the long-term economics of AI labs. The two chief executives sit on the supply side of the debt stack described in [[2026-10-09#10|Broadcom's own $50B financing for OpenAI chips]] and tested by [[2026-10-09#11|Firmus Grid's failed IPO]].
items.title: Broadcom and Intel CEOs say capital access, not chips, may become AI's bottleneck

items.summary: The investigation puts annual scam revenue at about $442B — larger than the global cocaine trade and than Denmark's GDP — with generative tools industrialising voice cloning, fake personas and translation, and Chinese-run operations spreading beyond fortified compounds in Southeast Asia. It is a measured estimate of criminal AI use rather than a model capability result.
items.title: Bloomberg: AI is scaling a ~$442B global scam economy

items.summary: Decart builds software that makes models run more efficiently and portably across different vendors' chips, plus real-time video and world generation (Lucy, Oasis). Anthropic was preferred bidder in August at roughly $6–7B and withdrew in September after due diligence; Nvidia had pursued it earlier. Neither party has confirmed. It would be the third AI company absorbed by a compute provider after [[2026-09-29#1|AMD's purchase of World Labs]] and the [[2026-10-11#9|Nvidia–Reflection AI talks]].
items.title: WSJ: Amazon in talks to buy Decart for about $7B after Anthropic walked away

items.summary: Bloomberg reports the model lab leading a seed round for a robot-AI company founded by a former Tencent scientist — its first notable outbound investment, and a move from language models into embodied AI rather than a new model release.
items.title: DeepSeek leads a $400M-valuation seed round in robotics startup Winverse AI

items.summary: A game director told the team the project moves to an "AI first" production plan with all art "generated with full AI workflows"; the release had already slipped from November to March. Epic's communications director said the company is "embracing AI-accelerated development". It is the first major studio mandate to stop writing code by hand, reported from internal sources rather than announced.
items.title: Bloomberg: Epic delays its Disney game and tells developers "no more hand-written code"

items.summary: CEO Cristiano Amon said AI companies are "starting to do phones" and are asking Qualcomm for silicon that can run 100-billion-parameter models locally and continuously by 2028, predicting "a battle of the agents" on-device. It is a stated customer requirement, not a shipping product — an order of magnitude above the 30B MoE in [[2026-09-23#6|the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6]].
items.title: Qualcomm says AI companies want phones running 100B-parameter models by 2028

lead: Microsoft unveiled Maia 300, its third-generation in-house accelerator with 288GB of HBM4 and 18TB/s of bandwidth, claiming 7x the rack-scale token throughput of Maia 200 and 40% more tokens per megawatt than leading GPU systems, as its primary AI inference platform from 2027.
window: 12 Oct 07:00 → 13 Oct 07:00 JST (+ late catches from 11 Oct)
